findings.evidence: `rg` hits: lines 36, 100, and 127 are `@[expose] def`; lines 39-42, 104-107, 137-152 provide the stated API lemmas.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from lines 36, 100, and 127; keep downstream computation through the exported characteristic lemmas, adding any missing lemma instead of making consumers unfold the definitions.
findings.issue: `GenLoop.map`, `HomotopyGroup.map`, and `HomotopyGroup.mapHom` all expose their bodies with `@[expose]` even though the file provides `map_apply`, `map_mk`, `mapHom_apply`, `map_one`, and `map_mul` as the intended API.

findings.evidence: `rg -n "mapHom_(id|comp)|mapHom.*comp|mapHom.*id"` finds no bundled functoriality lemmas; the only identity/composition lemmas are `map_id_apply` at line 110 and `map_comp_apply` at line 118.
findings.fix: Add simp/extensional lemmas such as `mapHom_id` and `mapHom_comp` stating equality of monoid homomorphisms, proved by `MonoidHom.ext` from the existing pointwise lemmas.
findings.issue: `mapHom` has no bundled identity or composition lemmas, so users of the positive-dimensional group-valued functor only get pointwise `map_id_apply` and `map_comp_apply` for the underlying function.

summary: The public surface is too open and the bundled homomorphism API is incomplete for functorial use. Fixing these does not require changing the mathematical construction.
